blocks.text: 16. This commandment the man kept not, but was disobedient to God, being led astray by the angel who, for the great gifts of God which He had given to man, was envious and jealous of him, [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-51] and both brought himself to nought and made man sinful, persuading him to disobey the commandment of God. So the angel, becoming by his falsehood the author and originator of sin, himself was struck down, having offended against God, and man he caused to be cast out from Paradise. And, because through the guidance of his disposition he apostatized and departed from God, he was called Satan, according to the Hebrew word; that is, Apostate: [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-52] a but he is also called Slanderer. Now God cursed the serpent which carried and conveyed the Slanderer; and this malediction came on the beast himself and on the angel hidden and concealed in him, even on Satan; and man He put away from His presence, removing him and making him to dwell on the way to Paradise [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-53] at that time; because Paradise receiveth not the sinful.

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-51.text: IV, lxvi. 2; ἔκτοτε γὰρ ἀποστάτης ὁ ἀγγελος οὗτος καὶ ἐχθρός. ἀφ᾽ ὅτε ἐζήλωσε τὸ πλάσμα τοῦ θεοῦ : V, xxiv. 4: “ Invidens homini, apostata a divina factus est lege: invidia enim aliena est a Deo. ” Cf. Wisd. ii. 24 : φθόνῳ δὲ διαβόλου θάνατος εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον .

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-52.text: V, xxi. 2: “ Satana enim verbum Hebraicum apostatam significat. ” Cf. Just. Mart. Dial. 103.

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-53.text: Cf. Gen. iii. 24 : κατῴκισεν αὐτὸν ἀπέναντι τοῦ παραδείσου τῆς τρυφῆς . Perhaps “the way” comes from “the way of the tree of life” in the same verse.
